skill.name: use-gemini-for-code-analysis
skill.description: Calls Gemini CLI to analyze large repositories, identify architecture patterns, trace feature implementations, and return raw results for review.
skill.summary: Repository-wide code analysis through Gemini CLI.

security_audit.summary: Most Markdown backtick findings are false positives around option names or fence delimiters. The actual Gemini command examples are confirmed because they run an external CLI across all files. Semantic review found full-repository disclosure, a confirmation-bypass flag, and unfiltered raw-output forwarding; no prompt injection attempt was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before --all-files. Document that source code may leave the local environment, and offer scoped path analysis first.
Remove --yolo from default guidance. Require interactive approval for Gemini commands and document when bypassing prompts is forbidden.
Add a review step before returning Gemini output. Redact secrets and warn about model-generated instructions from the external tool.
Use fixed command templates with quoted arguments. Avoid shell interpolation of user-supplied text.

semantic_findings.title: Whole Repository Disclosure to External AI CLI

semantic_findings.title: Confirmation Bypass Flag Recommended

semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The text explicitly names --yolo and says it skips confirmation. The non-destructive caveat lowers severity but does not remove the risk.

content.user_title: Analyze Large Codebases with Gemini CLI
content.value_statement: Large repositories are hard to map quickly with manual search. This skill routes focused architecture and code-pattern questions through Gemini CLI for broad repository analysis.
actual_capabilities: Build prompts for repository-wide Gemini CLI analysis.
Ask Gemini to inspect all files with the --all-files option.
Request architecture, module, and data-flow summaries.
Trace feature implementations across related files.
Scan for performance, security, and code-quality concerns.
Return Gemini CLI output without additional interpretation.
limitations: Requires Gemini CLI, shell access, and valid authentication.
May send repository content to an external AI service.
Does not redact secrets or sensitive source code by itself.
Does not verify Gemini results before returning them.

use_cases.title: Map a New Repository
use_cases.description: Map major modules, data flow, and design decisions before making a first change.

use_cases.title: Triage Security Review
use_cases.description: Ask Gemini to scan for suspicious patterns across a large project before manual review.

use_cases.title: Trace Feature Impact
use_cases.description: Trace a feature across files to find integration points and likely change areas.

prompt_templates.title: Map the Repository
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Gemini CLI to analyze the whole repository. Summarize the main directories, major components, and how data moves through the system.

prompt_templates.title: Find a Pattern
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to find every use of [pattern or library]. Include example locations, common usage shapes, and possible problems.

prompt_templates.title: Trace a Feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Gemini CLI to trace [feature]. Identify entry points, data models, services, UI paths, tests, and external integrations.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Architecture Risks
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Gemini CLI to analyze [subsystem]. Report coupling, performance risks, security-sensitive paths, and refactoring options with supporting file references.

output: Data flow between client, service, and storage layers.
Directories and files that support each area.

output_examples.output: A feature map covering entry points, middleware, session handling, storage paths, integrations, and related tests.

output: Areas with expensive queries or repeated work.
Files that contain the relevant logic.

best_practices: Confirm that repository contents can be shared with Gemini before using all-file analysis.
Scope prompts to the smallest useful area when sensitive files may be present.
Review Gemini output before acting on recommendations or sharing results.
anti_patterns: Do not use --yolo when command effects or data exposure are unclear.
Do not send secrets, private keys, or customer data to Gemini through this workflow.
Do not treat raw Gemini output as verified security evidence without manual review.

faq.question: Does this skill require Gemini CLI?
faq.answer: Yes. The local environment must have Gemini CLI installed, authenticated, and available in the shell.

faq.question: Does it edit files?
faq.answer: The skill is designed for analysis. The documented examples ask Gemini to inspect files and return findings, not modify code.

faq.question: Can it analyze private repositories?
faq.answer: It can, but private code may be sent to Gemini. Get approval and scope the analysis before use.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The report declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code when they can run shell commands.

faq.question: Will results be fully accurate?
faq.answer: No. Gemini output can miss context or make mistakes. Treat results as leads for manual review.

faq.question: Can I limit the files analyzed?
faq.answer: Yes. Prefer focused paths or specific questions when full repository analysis is not needed.
